description:
FOUND s490 (Fable), review probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s490/probes/t6b/p1878.pl lines 3-5; minimal:

  $@ = { code => 5 };  print "E:$@->{code}\n";     # perl: E:5      PCL main ab4da8b4: E:HASH(0x1)->{code}
  $@ = [9];            print "F:$@->[0]\n";        # perl: F:9      PCL: F:ARRAY(0x1)->[0]
  my $h = { code => 6 }; print "$h->{code}\n";       # 6 on both (the ordinary-variable path is right)
  $_ = { code => 7 };   print "$_->{code}\n";       # 7 on both

So the interpolation scanner continues into `->[` / `->{` after an identifier and after `$_`, but not after `$@`.  perl continues after ANY scalar it interpolates (probe the rest of the punctuation set before fixing: `$!` `$0` `$1` `$&` `$,` `$/` `$;` -- perl interpolates only some of them at all; the #451 note in CLAUDE.md s438g says the SUBSCRIPT set is its own, measured character by character, and this is the ARROW set -- measure it the same way, do not reuse either table unprobed).

WHERE: Pl/InterpScan.pm, the `$` arm (standing rule: interpolation scanning happens there or not at all; contract docs/interp-scan.md).  #451 (s438g) widened the same arm for a direct subscript (`"$?[1]"`); this is the sibling for an arrow chain.  Emission-changing (generation bump, corpus-diff, the Pl/ row of WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN).

WHY IT MATTERS: exception OBJECTS and hashes in $@ are the modern die idiom (Try::Tiny-free code, `die { code => ..., msg => ... }`), and the wrong text is plausible-looking output, not a crash.

GUARD: Pl/t/punct-array-glob-01.t (the #451 file) or the InterpScan guard file -- whichever is faster by `prove --timer`.

=== DONE (s491a) ===

SHIPPED.  Pl/InterpScan.pm (the ONE `$` arm, per the standing rule) plus the
runtime half the widening exposed; guard = 5 rows in Pl/t/punct-array-glob-01.t
(the #451 file, 3.1 s wall vs interp-scan-01.t -- measured), 3 of them FAIL on
an extraction of 337f6a23 and 2 are the must-not-break direction.

THE ARROW SET, MEASURED CHARACTER BY CHARACTER (perl 5.40.3; generator
scratch/s491a/probes/gen1846.pl, 120 rows, table
scratch/s491a/probes/p1846-set.perl.table).  For each name: T1 `"$N->{k}"`,
T2 `"$N->[0]"`, T3 `"$N->meth"`, T4 `"$N[0]"` (the #451 control).  TOOK = the
literal text was consumed, LIT = it survived, ERR = the deref was attempted and
died (a read-only match variable; also "consumed").

  name    T1 ->{}  T2 ->[]  T3 ->m  T4 [0]      name   T1   T2   T3   T4
  @       TOOK     TOOK     LIT     TOOK        -      TOOK TOOK LIT  TOOK
  !       TOOK     TOOK     LIT     TOOK        <      TOOK TOOK LIT  TOOK
  ?       TOOK     TOOK     LIT     TOOK        >      TOOK TOOK LIT  TOOK
  .       TOOK     ERR      LIT     TOOK        (      TOOK TOOK LIT  TOOK
  /       TOOK     TOOK     LIT     TOOK        )      TOOK TOOK LIT  TOOK
  \       TOOK     TOOK     LIT     TOOK        [      TOOK TOOK LIT  TOOK
  &       ERR      ERR      LIT     TOOK        ]      TOOK TOOK LIT  TOOK
  '       ERR      ERR      LIT     TOOK        ~      TOOK TOOK LIT  TOOK
  `       ERR      ERR      LIT     TOOK        "      TOOK TOOK LIT  TOOK
  +       ERR      ERR      LIT     TOOK        $      TOOK TOOK LIT  TOOK
  ;       TOOK     TOOK     LIT     TOOK        ^W     TOOK TOOK LIT  TOOK
  ,       TOOK     TOOK     LIT     TOOK        0      TOOK TOOK LIT  TOOK
  |       TOOK     TOOK     LIT     TOOK        1      ERR  ERR  LIT  TOOK
  :       TOOK     TOOK     LIT     TOOK        _      TOOK ERR  LIT  TOOK
  %       TOOK     TOOK     LIT     TOOK
  =       TOOK     TOOK     LIT     TOOK

So: T1/T2 are consumed for EVERY name, T3 for NONE (perl never calls a method
inside a string), and T4 -- the BARE subscript -- is consumed for every name
too, which is the #653 gap, NOT this task (PCL's $PUNCT_ARRAY_SUBSCRIPT is
narrower on purpose).  After the fix, PCL agrees with perl on all 90 T1/T2/T3
rows; the 15 remaining extent diffs are all T4 (`( ) , : ; @ [ ] ^W ` \ " ' |
$`), i.e. #653's family, and the `^W` and `( ) [ ] :` members are new
information for it.

OTHER SHAPES (scratch/s491a/probes/p1846-shapes.pl, perl side beside it): a
blank before the arrow ENDS the reference; `->` alone, `->(1)`, `->@*` (without
postderef_qq) and `->meth` stay literal; a braced NAME closes the reference
(`"${r}->{k}"` is literal, perl's own asymmetry) and so does `${^NAME}`; a
braced EXPRESSION takes it; the REGEX consumer takes it too (`/$@->{k}/`
matches) and so does a heredoc.  `$#ar->[0]` is the one shape left diverging --
FILED as #1971 with its fix shape.

THE FIX: one predicate `_arrow_next($text, $ev)` beside `_scan_chain`,
asked by the three arms that had no chain at all (single-punctuation magic,
`$^W` caret magic, bare `$$`).  It is NOT the #451 subscript table and NOT
Pl::Parser's %PUNCT_ARRAY_CHARS: three sets, three questions, and the comment
in InterpScan says so.

THE RUNTIME HALF, found by the breaking-case probe: taking the arrow after
`$$`/`$^W` hands a NUMBER to the container resolver, which had a STRING
symbolic-ref arm and no number arm -- the value fell through to SBCL's GETHASH
and the program died with a raw CL type error ("Value of pcl::h in
(sb-impl::gethash3 k h nil) is 204316, not a hash-table"), untrappable in perl
terms.  That divergence was ALREADY there in CODE with no string in sight
(`my $v = $$->{k}` crashed the same way on main).  perl stringifies a number
and treats it as a symbolic reference, so one predicate `%p-symref-name`
(string -> itself, number -> its stringification, else nil) now answers for
p-gethash-deref / p-aref-deref / p-ensure-hashref / p-ensure-arrayref.  The
SCALAR deref `${…}` is deliberately NOT routed through it: a number there is
ambiguous with a collapsed hard ref in the box model, ruled in #505/#551, and
those arms say so.  Probe: all 7 rows of scratch/s491a/probes/p1846-symref.pl
now identical to perl.

BARS: corpus-diff 337f6a23 = emission IDENTICAL across 111 files, silent drops
5 unchanged (scratch/s491a/log-corpus-diff-m2.txt); emission-ab --shapes over
the lib shims (27 files) and the cpan module population (99 files) = SAME,
0 DIFF, 0 RCDIFF (log-emission-ab-m2.txt).  No corpus carries the shape, so by
the s371 rule the PROBES AND GUARDS ARE THE BAR.  Targeted gate (13 files
naming interpolation / deref / magic vars): 585 rows PASS.  ir-spec 3.2b gains
the normative arrow-set paragraph and 2.3c the number-is-a-symbolic-ref
sentence; the `$#` divergence is recorded beside its bullet.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing, found at the s473t6b review): in a double-quoted string an ARROW CHAIN after the punctuation variable `$@` is left LITERAL -- `"$@->{code}"` prints `HASH(0x1)->{code}` and `"$@->[0]"` prints `ARRAY(0x1)->[0]` where perl prints the element (the everyday exception-object idiom `die { code => 5 }` ... `print "failed: $@->{code}"`)
